title: The otter
text: Day {day}, {city}. You pet the otter. It was worth it. Three days later the nick on your finger is hot and the fever arrives at 3 am. The hospital is very clean and very confused.
mitigatedText: Day {day}, {city}. You pet the otter. It was worth it. That night you clean the nick on your finger, and when it goes hot two days later the antibiotics are already in the bag. You keep your week.

title: What gives?
text: While lifting the bag onto the train, something in your upper back gives out. For the next ten days, existence is suffering.

title: Baggage carousel, one wheel short
text: Your suitcase comes around the carousel on three wheels and a stump. The airline offers a form. The form does nothing.

title: Delayed baggage
text: Everyone else's bag comes out. Yours is, according to the app, still in the departure city, having a nice time. The laptop is on your shoulder; everything else is somewhere else for a while. No clean clothes, no kitchen, no gym until it shows up.

title: The kettle
text: The travel kettle boils, then does not stop, then detonates. You get second-degree burns across your wrist. The hotel has a kettle. It always had a kettle.

title: Food poisoning
text: Day {day}, {city}. What rhymes with cryarrhea and is coming out of you right now? You spend two days learning the bathroom tile pattern by heart.
mitigatedText: Day {day}, {city}. That lukewarm salmon mayo bowl was a mistake. The probiotics fight back. One rough night, not two days.

title: Cancelled on arrival
text: You land in {city}. The host has cancelled 'due to unforeseen circumstances', which is to say a better booking. It is 6 pm, everything you own is on your back, and the only hotel with a room is across town. You get there. You do not enjoy getting there.

title: Left behind
text: Two hours out of {city} you realize your {item} is still in the room. The host 'will take a look'. The host does not take a look.
mitigatedText: You do the packing-cube count before you leave {city}. Everything has a place; everything is in its place.

title: The swarm
text: Sunset in {city}. The mosquitoes arrive like a scene from Jumanji. You wake up with a constellation on each ankle and the sleep of a hunted animal.
mitigatedText: Sunset in {city}. The mosquitoes arrive. The net goes up and you sleep like a baby. A baby desired by a hundred flying needles, just out of reach.

title: Jet lag
text: Six or more time zones in one leg. For three days you are awake at 4 am and asleep in meetings. The body keeps its own calendar.
mitigatedText: Six or more time zones in one leg. Melatonin at night and sun lamp on at 7. The body grumbles and gets in line.

title: Wind day
text: The wind arrives promptly at 2 pm. Everyone in {city} disappears to the water. You watch enviously from the shoreline.
mitigatedText: The wind arrives promptly at 2 pm. You rig up. Best day of the month.

title: Check-in scale
text: The airline scale reads a number and the agent reads it back to you like a diagnosis. Fifty one pounds is not fifty pounds.

title: Oktoberfest
text: Opening weekend. A tent, a prost, another prost, a brass band that has no right to go this hard. You lose a day and gain a story.

title: It rains
text: It rains in {city}. Not dramatically. Continuously. Everything you own is slightly damp.
mitigatedText: It rains in {city}. The shell goes on. You are the only dry person at the bus stop.

mitigatedTextBy.umbrella: It rains in {city}. The umbrella which you have resented carrying until now finally earns its keep.

title: Sunburn
text: You forgot the sunscreen. Your shoulders will remember it for a week.
mitigatedText: SPF 30 in the morning. The UV index remains an afterthought.

title: The upstairs neighbor
text: The apartment above yours in {city} is either a nightclub or a family of tap dancers.
mitigatedText: The apartment above yours is a nightclub. Earplugs in. You hear nothing until the alarm.

title: Wildlife
text: A moose or a stag stands in the trail outside {city} and does not move. Neither do you. Highlight of the month.

title: A good day
text: Day {day}, {city}. Nothing goes wrong. The coffee is right, the light is right, the work day hums on by.

title: No wifi
text: The listing said wifi. The listing meant a router, unplugged, in a drawer. You hotspot the phone and pray to the tower on the hill.

title: The laundromat
text: The laundromat in {city} returns everything except one sock and your favourite t-shirt. Neither is ever seen again.

title: The host
text: Your host in {city} leaves bread, local cheese and a handwritten map of the neighborhood. The map is wrong but the cheese is perfect.

title: Someone you know
text: A friend from two cities ago is, by coincidence, in {city} this week. Dinner turns into a weekend.

title: Delayed
text: The flight to {city} boards, sits, deboards, and then leaves four hours late. You learn the gate area's every outlet. None of them work.

title: Upgraded
text: At the gate the agent looks at you, looks at the screen, and hands you a new boarding pass. Row two. You do not ask why.

title: The window seat
text: The train to {city} runs along a lake, then a valley, then a lake again. You get nothing done and regret none of it.

title: One cable short
text: The watch cable is in the last hotel. The watch dies on day three and you become a person who does not know their current step count.
mitigatedText: Every cable has a pouch and every pouch has a place. You leave {city} with all of them.

title: A real gym
text: {city} has a real gym, with real weights, and a day pass costs less than a coffee. Arm day, finally.

title: The cafe
text: You find the cafe in {city}. Not a cafe: THE cafe. You will structure the rest of the stay around it.

title: Running low
text: Everything in the bag has been worn twice. You rotate the least offensive shirt to the front and hope for a laundromat.

title: The monitor
text: The air monitor blinks red in {city}. Radon: the granite under the town has been quietly exhaling for ten thousand years. You open a window. Problem solved.

title: The headache
text: You have had a headache since you arrived in {city}. Old building, shut windows, and you do not know why.

title: The card declines
text: The card declines in {city}. You try it again. It declines again, but slower, as if to make a point.

title: A good day
text: Day {day}, {city}. Nothing goes wrong. The coffee is right, the light is right, the mountains stand tall in the distance.

title: A good day
text: Day {day}, {city}. Nothing goes wrong. The coffee is right, the light is right, the warm beach beckons.

title: The taxi dies
text: Twenty minutes from the terminal the taxi coughs, rolls onto the shoulder and goes quiet. You pay, grab the suitcase and run.

title: The Airbnb knife
text: {city}. The listing said 'fully equipped kitchen'. The kitchen has one knife and it was from the dollar store. Tomatoes will be bruised, not sliced. Every cut here needs to be more precise than you would like.
mitigatedText: {city}. The listing said 'fully equipped kitchen'. The kitchen has one knife and it was from the dollar store. Good thing you brought your own. Crisis averted, tomatoes saved.

mitigatedTextBy.adventure: {city}. The listing said 'fully equipped kitchen'. The kitchen has one knife and it was from the dollar store. You unroll the adventure kit. Crisis averted, tomatoes saved.
mitigatedTextBy.kitchenknife: {city}. The listing said 'fully equipped kitchen'. The kitchen has one knife and it was from the dollar store. Yours comes out of its sheath. Crisis averted, tomatoes saved.

title: The chocolate
text: {city}. A rare find! A bar of chocolate from the corner shop. By morning your stomach is not happy. You go to throw the wrapper away and stop: the inside of the packaging is dotted with tiny brown capsules, stuck in neat rows. Cockroach eggs.
mitigatedText: {city}. A rare find! A bar of chocolate from the corner shop. By morning your stomach is not happy, and by afternoon, with the probiotics from the medicine kit kick in. You go to throw the wrapper away and stop: the inside of the packaging is dotted with tiny brown capsules in neat rows. Cockroach eggs.

title: The drone and the law
text: {city}. Two police officers watch the drone land. One of them has been filming you filming. Drones are not legal here, they explain, kindly, while writing. The fine comes out of the travel fund. The footage was good, though.

title: The permit you did not have
text: {city}. A ranger appears from nowhere, the way rangers do. Flying here needs a permit, and the permit needs a form, and the form needs three weeks. The fine needs only your card.

title: The jellyfish
text: {city}. Warm water, a long swim out, and something soft brushes your face. The sting lands on your lips. Within a minute they are twice their size and you cannot say the word 'jellyfish' to the lifeguard, only point at your mouth. It hurts more than anything has any right to.
mitigatedText: {city}. Warm water, a long swim out, and something soft brushes your face. The sting lands on your lips and they double in size in a minute. The first-aid kit has the antihistamines; by evening you can say 'jellyfish' again, slowly.

title: The tick
text: {city}. Heather, bracken, a long day on the hill. In the shower you find a small dark passenger behind your knee, legs waving. You try to pull it out yourself with tweezers, but you just end up massacring it while it's still inside you. The next day you go to the doctor to get the rest removed.
mitigatedText: {city}. Heather, bracken, a long day on the hill. In the shower you find a small dark passenger behind your knee. The tick tool from the first-aid kit has it out whole in one pull. You check the bite for a ring anyway, every day, for three weeks.

title: The flu
text: {city}. It starts as a scratchy throat on a video call and by nightfall you are shivering under every blanket the place owns. Three days lost staring at the ceiling. The city carries on outside the window without you.
mitigatedText: {city}. A scratchy throat on a video call, shivers by nightfall. The medicine kit has the good paracetamol and the electrolytes; two rough days instead of three, and you keep the soup down.

title: Museum day
text: {city}. You spend the afternoon in {museum} and come out three hours later blinking, with a postcard you will never send. Worth it.

title: Sand flies
text: {city}. A perfect evening strolling the beach. The next morning your ankles and shins are a constellation of red welts. Sand flies. Nobody warned you because everyone assumed you'd know.
mitigatedText: {city}. A perfect evening strolling the beach. You sprayed the ankles out of habit. In the morning: two bites. The couple at the next table look like they were eaten alive.

title: A laundromat
text: {city}. Behind the bakery, a laundromat with working machines and a bench in the sun. $15, ninety minutes, a whole bag of clean everything. The small victories are the ones you remember.

title: Dolphins
text: {city}. Out on the water before the wind picks up, and a fin, then three, then a whole pod cutting through the swell thirty feet out.

title: The long walk
text: {city}. What started out as a walk around the block turned into a five-hour adventure: a market, a hill, a neighborhood that was not on the map, a bakery that saved the day. Your legs file a complaint. Everything else is delighted.

title: Matcha soft serve
text: {city}. A stand by the station sells matcha soft serve so green it looks fake. It is not fake. You have two. This does not get logged in your health journal.

title: The ice cave
text: {city}. Crampons on, into the glacier. The ice is a new shade of blue and the cave breathes cold on the back of your neck. You emerge a new person.

title: A new friend
text: {city}. On the way back, {animal} decides you are worth a closer look. Ten minutes later you have a friend for the afternoon. The best company on the trail does not talk.

title: Ocean swim
text: {city}. A long swim down the shoreline, the town sliding past on the right, nothing in your head for once. You come out salt-crusted and inspired.

title: The shark
text: {city}. A long swim down the shoreline, the town sliding past on the right. People on the beach start shouting and waving, and it takes a while to understand they are waving at you. Behind you, a fin, keeping pace. You swim to shore faster than you thought was possible. It follows to the shallows and turns away.

title: The casino
text: {city}. You went for a walk and stumble upon a casino. The casino has air conditioning and no clocks.

title: Batman Origin Story
text: {city}. You wake to a scattering of small dark pellets on the pillow, next to your face. Not seeds. The cabin has an unexpected resident in the rafters.
